source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning (ICE)
finding: Adds irrelevant tokens to multi-hop questions to raise extraneous load while holding the task fixed. Only the strongest model shows a clean load curve.
numbers: 200 questions x 10 replications, 5 models. Gemini-2.0-Flash exact match: control 0.85, 20% junk 0.82, 50% 0.78, 80% 0.72; slope -0.003 per % load, p<0.001.
limits: Preprint, single author. Load is defined by junk share, not by any rating scale. Attention weights and cosine similarity are named as measures but the behavioural results use only accuracy.
agent_relevance: Load can be measured by accuracy drop under controlled junk. No ratings needed.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning (ICE)
finding: Length alone did not explain the drop: a length-matched control without junk matched the clean control.
numbers: Gemini Long Control 0.82 vs Control 0.85, p=0.45. Residue (task-switch) condition 0.78, extra decline not significant (p=0.12).
limits: Non-significant residue effect; the paper still reads it as support. Treat as untested.
agent_relevance: Separating junk from length is the right control when we use tokens as a load proxy.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning (ICE)
finding: Small models failed at the clean baseline, so extraneous load could not be tested. A floor effect: intrinsic load swamped everything.
numbers: Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, Mistral-7B all 0% exact match in every condition including control. GPT-4o-0613 control 0.65, 80% load 0.55, slope -0.002, p=0.07 (ns).
limits: About 32% of GPT-4o outputs omitted a final answer (12% after structured prompting), so its numbers are confounded by format failure.
agent_relevance: A load measure needs a task the model can solve at baseline. Check the clean control first.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning (ICE)
finding: Intermediate-hop recall gives a finer process measure than final answer alone.
numbers: Gemini hop recall 0.90 control to 0.75 at 80% saturation; GPT-4o 0.80 to 0.65. Residue correlated with embedding similarity: r=0.42 (Gemini), r=0.35 (GPT-4o).
limits: Post hoc power 0.85 Gemini, 0.78 GPT-4o. A correlation is not a manipulation check.
agent_relevance: Log intermediate steps as a second load readout, like a secondary-task probe.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive Load-Aware Inference: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Optimizing the Token Economy of LLMs (CLAI)
finding: Maps intrinsic, extraneous and germane load to LLM metrics: intrinsic = a 1-10 complexity score the model rates; extraneous = low-attention or redundant tokens; germane = productive reasoning tokens tied to a token budget.
numbers: Stage 1 sets a token budget (e.g. 50 tokens for easy, 500 for hard). Stage 2 cleans context. Stage 3 reasons within budget.
limits: Metrics are proposed, mostly model self-rating and attention scores. No check against any human load measure.
agent_relevance: A template for a load-estimate step that sets a token budget. It is self-report by the model, so it needs validating.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive Load-Aware Inference: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Optimizing the Token Economy of LLMs (CLAI)
finding: Reported token savings at near equal accuracy on math (zero-shot prompt version).
numbers: Llama-3-70B GSM8K: CoT 92.5% at 485 tokens vs CLAI-Prompt 92.3% at 310 (-36.1%). MATH: 53.9% at 812 vs 53.5% at 525 (-35.3%).
limits: Single-author preprint. Round numbers, no variance or seeds. Tables use different base models, so cross-table comparison is unsafe. Unreplicated.
agent_relevance: Budgeting tokens by estimated difficulty is a cheap thing to test ourselves.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive Load-Aware Inference: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Optimizing the Token Economy of LLMs (CLAI)
finding: Distilled version (CLAI-Tune, Llama-3-8B student trained on teacher-generated data) cut tokens further and slightly raised scores.
numbers: GSM8K 91.5% at 255 tokens (-43.3%) vs speculative decoding 90.1% at 450. MATH 52.1% at 440 (-43.6%) vs 50.2%. Long-context QA: CLAI-Prompt 69.3 at 980 tokens vs full context 65.2 at 4096 (4.2x), LLMLingua 68.1.
limits: Same caveats. Teacher data is synthetic and the paper admits dependence on teacher quality.
agent_relevance: Context cleaning (drop low-relevance text) may help accuracy as well as cost.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive Load-Aware Inference: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Optimizing the Token Economy of LLMs (CLAI)
finding: Authors warn that CLT does not mean fewer tokens is always better: germane effort must stay.
numbers: No number.
limits: A stated design view, not a tested result.
agent_relevance: Matches our rule to use tokens as a signal, not as a target to minimise.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: One irrelevant sentence added to grade-school math problems sharply cuts accuracy. The best measure is macro accuracy (a base problem counts only if solved under every distractor).
numbers: Fewer than 30% of base problems solved under all distractor variants for code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003. Base-problem accuracy with CoT for text-davinci-003 was 80.0.
limits: Old models (2022 class). Newer models may do better; ICE and CogniLoad suggest the effect remains.
agent_relevance: Macro-style robustness (same item, many distractors) is a stricter load test than average accuracy.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: Scaffolds that cut distraction: self-consistency, exemplars showing distractors, and a one-line instruction to ignore irrelevant information.
numbers: Self-consistency over 20 samples raised micro accuracy by more than 11 points (35.5 for 0-CoT); correct answer in the 20 samples for 99.7%; best macro accuracy still only 45%. The instruction 'Feel free to ignore irrelevant information' helped; 'Solve grade school math problems' alone did not.
limits: Instruction and exemplar effects did not hurt clean GSM8K (CoT 59.3 to 60.3).
agent_relevance: A cheap guardrail: tell the agent to ignore irrelevant material, and sample several times when load is high.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: Distractors that share roles or numbers with the question hurt most.
numbers: Text-davinci-003 macro accuracy fell to 0 on problems with more than 2 reasoning steps when the irrelevant sentence had role overlap.
limits: Single model family.
agent_relevance: Extraneous load is not about length; similar-looking junk is worst.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad: A Synthetic Natural Language Reasoning Benchmark With Tunable Length, Intrinsic Difficulty, and Distractor Density
finding: Benchmark built on CLT with three separate dials: intrinsic difficulty d, distractor ratio rho (extraneous), task length N (germane proxy). 22 reasoning LLMs.
numbers: 100 puzzles per (d,N,rho) cell for open models (about 14,000 each); 10 per cell for Gemini-2.5, GPT-5 family, DeepSeek-R1-0528. 32K token cap.
limits: N as germane load is an analogy the authors state. Only deductive puzzles. Exact match scoring.
agent_relevance: The cleanest machine analogue of separating load types. Length is the main stressor.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad: A Synthetic Natural Language Reasoning Benchmark With Tunable Length, Intrinsic Difficulty, and Distractor Density
finding: Task length N is the strongest limit. Steepest fall between N=20 and N=50 for most models.
numbers: DS-Llama-70B 0.89 to 0.66; Qwen3-8B 0.71 to 0.40. At N=250 only gpt-5 (0.76) and o3 (0.68) exceed 0.50; most sit at 0.20-0.30.
limits: Proprietary models had 10 puzzles per cell, so noisier.
agent_relevance: Long chains of steps cost more than hard single steps. Cut chain length and carry state explicitly.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad: A Synthetic Natural Language Reasoning Benchmark With Tunable Length, Intrinsic Difficulty, and Distractor Density
finding: Distractor ratio gives a U shape, not a straight decline: worst at 25-50% distractors, better at high ratio.
numbers: gpt-5 0.97, 0.89, 0.91 across low, mid, high rho; gemini-2.5-flash-lite 0.38 to 0.53; Phi-4-reasoning-plus 0.59 to 0.45; EXAONE-Deep-32B 0.47 to 0.32. Quadratic rho term significant for most; 5 models show none.
limits: Direction differs between models. Reasons unproven.
agent_relevance: Models respond to load types differently, as humans do; one scalar load score would mislead.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad: A Synthetic Natural Language Reasoning Benchmark With Tunable Length, Intrinsic Difficulty, and Distractor Density
finding: Capacity thresholds per model: ECL50 (statements at 50% accuracy).
numbers: gpt-5 382.8, o3 356.9, gpt-5-mini 164.1, gemini-2.5-pro 153.3; Qwen3-1.7B and DS-Qwen-1.5B about 0. By d=5, 12 of 22 models below 50%. Both d and log10 N negative in every model's regression.
limits: Fits depend on the 32K cap and default decoding.
agent_relevance: A per-model load capacity can be measured by accuracy alone. We could calibrate our agent's step budget this way.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad: A Synthetic Natural Language Reasoning Benchmark With Tunable Length, Intrinsic Difficulty, and Distractor Density
finding: Failure types change with load: state-tracking errors under length, context overflow and format breaks for small models.
numbers: Qwen3-32B 2,541 state-tracking errors at N=250. gemini-2.5-flash overflowed on 280/350 samples at N=250 vs gpt-5 32/350. DS-Qwen-1.5B 605 other replies.
limits: Counts depend on the token cap.
agent_relevance: Error type is a diagnostic. Track it, not only accuracy.

source: Upadhayay, Behzadan, Karbasi (2024) Cognitive Overload Attack: Prompt Injection for Long Context
finding: Uses CLT framing: overload prompts make models drop safety behaviour.
numbers: Attack success up to 99.99% on GPT-4, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, Claude-3 Opus, Llama-3-70B-Instruct, Gemini-1.0-Pro, Gemini-1.5-Pro.
limits: Only the abstract page was read. Prompt design not seen. CLT link is an analogy; no separate load measurement.
agent_relevance: Heavy load can break guardrails. Keep guardrails outside the loaded context or re-check them at the end.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: The same tasks spread over several turns give worse results; mostly unreliability, little loss of aptitude.
numbers: Average drop 39% across six generation tasks, over 200,000 simulated conversations, top open and closed models. Models commit to early assumptions and do not recover.
limits: Only the abstract page was read. Not framed as CLT. Remedies not on the page.
agent_relevance: Accumulated history acts as extraneous load. Restart or summarise state rather than keep long histories.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Accuracy is best when the relevant item is at the start or end, and falls when it is in the middle, even for long-context models.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page (TACL 2023).
limits: Abstract page only. A position effect, not a load effect; ICE argues saturation is separate.
agent_relevance: Place key facts at the edges of the prompt.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models spend large token budgets on easy problems. Proposes outcome and process efficiency metrics; self-training shortens traces while keeping accuracy.
numbers: Evaluated on GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, AIME. No figures on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only; numbers not verified.
agent_relevance: Tokens spent against difficulty is a usable load-efficiency ratio, like relative condition efficiency in human work.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: In puzzles with controlled complexity, reasoning effort rises with complexity then falls while token budget remains, and accuracy collapses. Three regimes: plain models win low, reasoning models win medium, both fail high.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only. Critiques of this paper exist and were not checked here.
agent_relevance: Token count is not a monotone load signal: a drop in effort at the hardest items is a warning, not relief.

source: Scaling Competence, Shrinking Reasoning: Cognitive Signatures in Language Model Learning
finding: Treats reasoning tokens as working memory. Under RL training, reasoning length rises, peaks, then shrinks as the task is internalised; models keep accuracy with reasoning off.
numbers: PPO, GRPO, REINFORCE; 100 iterations x 32 rollouts; models include Phi-4 (13B), GPT-4o-mini, o4-mini; tasks GSM8K, CommonsenseQA, low-resource code MCQ. No numbers in the text, only figures.
limits: The paper does not measure cognitive load. Model size listed inconsistently (7B vs 23B). Answer accuracy rose while trace correctness fell.
agent_relevance: Falling token use after practice mirrors automation of schemas; token count reflects skill level as well as task difficulty.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) United Minds or Isolated Agents? Exploring Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker)
finding: A multi-agent set-up built from CLT: split intrinsic load across specialist agents, manage coordination load with shared memory. Gains on reasoning-heavy tasks, losses on instruction-following.
numbers: LiveBench, Gemini-1.5-Pro: Math 75.3 vs 70.0 best baseline; Reasoning 44.7 vs 43.0; Instruction 81.8 vs 84.4. Flash-8B Instruction 68.1 vs 84.3. 16 of 25 paired comparisons significant (Holm, alpha 0.05); the 3 significant losses all instruction-following.
limits: Authors call it a functional analogy only. About 25 API calls per question vs 1 for a single agent. Greedy decoding.
agent_relevance: Extra structure pays on high-intrinsic tasks and costs on easy ones: gate scaffolding by estimated load.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) United Minds or Isolated Agents? Exploring Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker)
finding: Load proxies used only in a pilot: attention entropy and perplexity, not at runtime.
numbers: Attention entropy 4.44, 4.80, 5.04 for complexity levels 1-3. Perplexity on hard tasks 120.50, 88.97, 85.35 (falls with complexity); easy tasks 3.37 to 3.45. Tokens per question: IO about 650-710, CoThinker 13,558-14,323, MAD 12,389-16,104.
limits: Perplexity needs ground truth; attention entropy needs model internals. The authors say neither fits as runtime control. Perplexity moving the wrong way shows proxies can mislead.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that internal proxies disagree, as human measures do. Prefer behavioural readouts.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) United Minds or Isolated Agents? Exploring Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker)
finding: Token-constrained setting: structure helped more under a tight budget.
numbers: 8,192-token cap, greedy: Gemini-2.5 Math/Reasoning CoThinker 76.3/69.2 vs IO 59.3/31.0; GPT-4.1 40.0/70.8 vs 34.0/40.8. Ablation: dropping shared memory raised GPT-5-Nano from 55.97 to 62.36.
limits: Cross-model results partial; models that hide intermediate reasoning gain less from shared memory.
agent_relevance: Scaffold value depends on the backbone, so test it.

source: Beyond Accuracy: A Cognitive Load Framework for Mapping the Capability Boundaries of Tool-use Agents (ToolLoad-Bench)
finding: Splits tool-task difficulty into intrinsic load (solution-path structure, via a Tool Interaction Graph) and extraneous load (ambiguous task wording); finds sharp performance cliffs as load rises.
numbers: AAAI 2026. No numbers on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only. The claim of highly calibrated predictions is unchecked.
agent_relevance: Agent loops show cliffs rather than gentle decline: find the cliff for our tool use.

source: RecalibrateGPT: AI Fatigue Resilient Conversational Interfaces (2026)
finding: Human users of chat LLMs: five one-click operators cut perceived workload.
numbers: 12 advanced users; NASA-TLX = 2.7 reported as half of before; SUS 86.5.
limits: Tiny sample, no stated baseline or statistics on the page. Self-report only.
agent_relevance: Shows NASA-TLX still used for LLM interfaces. It rates the human, not the model.

source: GuideAI: A Real-time Personalized Learning Solution with Adaptive Interventions (2026)
finding: LLM tutor adapts content from biosensors (gaze, heart rate variability, posture, note-taking). NASA-TLX showed lower mental demand, frustration and effort.
numbers: Formative N=66; preliminary evaluation N=25. Learning gains 'statistically significant' with no figures.
limits: Abstract page only. Preliminary study. No account of how sensors map to a load estimate.
agent_relevance: An example of a physiology plus rating-scale loop steering an LLM. Our agent has no body, so token and error signals replace it.

source: Kosmyna et al. (2025) Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing
finding: EEG during essay writing: weaker connectivity with more tool use (brain-only strongest, search moderate, LLM weakest).
numbers: 54 participants in sessions 1-3, 18 in session 4; LLM users reported lowest essay ownership.
limits: Abstract page only. Small sample. EEG connectivity is not a validated load score.
agent_relevance: Warns that low measured load with an LLM can mean low engagement, not efficiency.

source: Mitigating Epistemic Debt in Generative AI-Scaffolded Novice Programming using Metacognitive Scripts (2026)
finding: Scaffolded AI with an Explanation Gate (LLM judge requires teach-back) lowered later failure compared with free AI use.
numbers: N=78 between-subjects; AI groups beat manual on functional utility (p<.001), no difference between them (p=.64); 77% unrestricted vs 39% scaffolded failed a 30-minute AI-blackout task.
limits: Abstract only; no load scale named. Claude 3.5 Sonnet was the backend.
agent_relevance: An LLM-as-judge gate is an in-loop scaffold control. Offloading versus outsourcing matters.

source: arXiv listing search: cognitive load + language model + NASA-TLX (5 results)
finding: No paper found that gives an LLM a NASA-TLX style questionnaire and validates it against behaviour. The search was narrow and API sources (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, arXiv API) were rate-limited, so this is a gap in my search, not proof of absence.
numbers: 5 results on the arXiv listing.
limits: Search coverage weak; WebSearch budget was exhausted after one call.
agent_relevance: Open question: does an LLM's self-rated difficulty predict its own error? Worth a small test.
